**Investment thesis**
---------------------

AMD at $259 per share on 5 November 2025 looks priced for perfection. I put fair value at roughly $56 and is why I'm avoiding. The gap rests son three things the market overestimates: durable growth, sustainable margins, and capital efficiency. My base case assumes 22% revenue growth, a steady 21% net margin, and sales-to-equity near 0.5x—well below the platform‑like economics the price implies today.

The market is underwriting a very different future: a long‑run 34.7% revenue CAGR, a 33.2% net margin and a 0.8x sales‑to‑equity ratio. That bundle would make AMD look more like a software platform than a fabless chip designer that must keep pace with Nvidia and depend on foundry supply. I do not see evidence for it.

Growth first. AI demand is real, but ramps are lumpy and constrained. Nvidia still dominates accelerators and export controls limit China‑bound SKUs. Recent prints point to moderation, not acceleration: AMD’s Data Center segment grew 22% year on year in Q3 2025, and management’s Q4 set‑up implies growth in the mid‑20s with gross margins in the mid‑50s, not a re‑acceleration to the mid‑30s that the market’s curve assumes. A 22% through‑cycle path is still strong, just not fantasy.

Margins next. To earn 33% net margins, AMD would need Nvidia‑like pricing power and lighter operating expense intensity. That jars with the firm’s heavy, ongoing R&D and software investment as it pushes ROCm and an accelerator roadmap (MI300/MI350 to MI400). 2024 GAAP gross margin was about 49%, and non‑GAAP gross margin was 54% in Q3 2025—good progress, but not the operating leverage one needs to convert into a one‑third net margin through the cycle. I anchor on a 21% steady margin instead.

Capital efficiency seals it. After big acquisitions, goodwill and intangibles keep equity large relative to sales. Working capital needs for accelerators are rising, and even with buybacks I expect sales‑to‑equity to settle near 0.5x rather than the market’s 0.8x. That matters because it governs how quickly the company can grow without bloating the balance sheet. History since the acquisitions sits in the mid‑0.3s to mid‑0.4s; 0.5x already assumes improvement.

When I run these economics through a DCF, I get an intrinsic value of $36–$66 per share, with a base case of $55.51. Even the 90th percentile of simulated values lands near $83—miles below the current price. The reverse‑DCF embedded in today’s quote delivers an expected IRR of just 5.6%, which is thin for a business facing this much competitive heat and execution risk.

Simple cross‑checks say the same. On prevailing numbers AMD trades at 72x earnings, 16x sales, and 5.6x book—rich even for AI‑exposed semis. If I apply a fair 12–16x earnings multiple to consensus EPS of about $5.10, I get $61–$82 per share, remarkably close to the DCF’s generous end and still far below $259. The signal is consistent: the equity embeds too much growth, too much margin, and too much efficiency.

Near‑term events could start to close the gap. In late January 2026 (unconfirmed), Q4 2025 results and 2026 guidance may frame growth in the low‑20s with net margins below 30%. That alone could take 20–30% off the share price as models converge with reality. Around mid‑March 2026 (unconfirmed), the annual report should reveal sales‑to‑equity nearer 0.45–0.50, undercutting 0.8x efficiency assumptions. Early 2026 results (around May, unconfirmed) are likely to show gross margins in the low‑to‑mid‑50s with elevated opex to fund the roadmap—again inconsistent with a one‑third net margin. These are tests I expect AMD to “pass” in a way that supports the bear case.

Risks to my view are clear. A faster AI cycle, stronger MI350/MI400 ramps, and broader ROCm adoption could pull demand forward and lift pricing and mix. In that upside world, growth could skew toward the mid‑30s, net margins could approach 30%+, and sales‑to‑equity could rise toward 0.7–0.8. Depending on how far those drivers run, the shares could justify the $220–$300 range—or even $300–$350 if accelerators and EPYC both surprise and sentiment re‑rates. I do not assign high probability to that path today, but I respect it.

What would change my mind? Consistent, audited evidence of capital efficiency trending to 0.7–0.8x; non‑GAAP gross margins holding mid‑50s while opex intensity falls, lifting the net margin toward the high‑20s; and proof that ROCm has become a sticky software layer that improves pricing power. If two of the three show up in reported numbers, I would raise my margin and efficiency anchors and soften the stance.

Until then, I stick with the simple story. AMD remains a high‑quality growth company moving toward early maturity, but the shares are valued as if it has already achieved platform economics. Strong execution can justify a premium; it cannot justify any price. I expect gravity—via guidance, reported efficiency, and disciplined multiples—to do the rest.

The story goes like this: Both AMD and Nvidia started the AI chip race around the same time, but their products weren't equal. Nvidia's GPUs provided significantly better performance than AMD's and it grew to dominate the AI chip market. AMD had a good run for a time, but after the stock peaked in March of 2024, it proceeded to lose 60% of its value and bottomed out in April 2025.

But it looks like things are changing.

Since April lows, AMD's stock has been performing just as well as Nvidia's, and up until recently, was actually performing noticably better.

So why is this? What's changed investors' minds?

Here's what's going on with AMD now, and what we can expect from the company in 2026 (and beyond):

Hyperscalers that build the giant data centers for training the most advanced AI models need GPUs at "rack-scale" capacities and in very large clusters that can support present & future projects requiring massive amounts of compute. While Nvidia is producing these chips as quickly as they can, they actually can't meet the level of demand they're seeing from customers.

This is an opportunity for AMD to offer a competing product and win market share from Nvdia without even needing to fight for it (since demand is already there). In March 2025, AMD acquired ZT Systems, a company that specializes in data center equipment (particularly for hyperscale cloud computing). That acquision, combined with the upcoming release of their newest MI400 series chips, will allow for a rack-scale solution that is expected to be a solid compeitor to Nvdia's next-gen Vera Rubin chips in terms of performance, but actually beat them when it comes to memory capacity and bandwidth.

So where AMD was previously just a budget-friendly option that couldn't really compete, they'll finally be entering the next round of the AI chip competition on a more level playing field. The revenue from these next-gen chip sales will likely start to be realized in Q2 or Q3 of 2026.

To get an idea of the potential growth AMD can see when their chips are recognized as equals in many ways to Nvdia's, take a look at each company's revenue numbers in Q2 2025.

*   AMD reported $3.2 billion in Q2 data center revenue 
*   Nvidia reported $41.1 billion in Q2 data center revenue 

If AMD could match Nvidia's scale with their MI400 series chips, it would mean a nearly 1300% increase from current quarterly data center revenue. Now that's a tall order, but even being able to fill just a quarter of what Nvidia is currently able to supply to its customers would represent more than a 300% data center revenue increase for AMD.

But that's _next_ year, what can we expect in the meantime for the rest of _this_ year?

Earlier this year, AMD announced they were releasing their MI350 series accelerators in mid 2025. These chips offer a 4x improvement in compute and 35x improvement in AI inference over their predecessors (MI300). "Inference" is becoming increasingly more important for AI models because its a measure of how well they can deliver real-world value by analyzing _new_ data and making predicitions & decisions from it. In other words, more inference means higher levels of "learned intelligence," and thus, smarter and more capable AIs.

These chips are designed to go head-to-head with Nvidia's Blackwell series chips, and once again, outperform when it comes to memory and bandwidth. While not shown in the table below, the B200 chips are 25x more efficient than their previous generation which makes electricity costs much lower for customers. The MI350 energy efficiency wasn't disclosed at the time of the announcement.

Although they're not viable for rack-scale levels of integration within datacenters, these chips still fill an important hole in the market.

In late July 2025, AMD announced that it would raise the price of its MI350 chips from $15,000 to $25,000 - a massive 67% price hike. This indicates how strong the demand is for this hardware and how much customers are willing to pay for it. Price hikes like these are expected to result in significant increases in revenue that appear in Q3 and Q4 earnings reports later this year - all while investors and AMD customers wait for the real showstopper (MI400) next year.

At just a $250B market cap, AMD has significant room to grow. Now that it's adjusted its strategy and is meeting customers where demand is highest, it's created a perfect setup for itself to experience incredible revenue growth over the next few years.

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Updated 3 min read

In this article: 

* [StockStory Top Pick](https://stockstory.org/high-quality/top-6-to-buy-this-week?partner=yahoo&utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=content_ticker&utm_campaign=contenthighqualitystock)

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Updated 3 min read

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Updated 3 min read

In this article: 

* [StockStory Top Pick](https://stockstory.org/high-quality/top-6-to-buy-this-week?partner=yahoo&utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=content_ticker&utm_campaign=contenthighqualitystock)

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Updated 3 min read

In this article: 

* [StockStory Top Pick](https://stockstory.org/high-quality/top-6-to-buy-this-week?partner=yahoo&utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=content_ticker&utm_campaign=contenthighqualitystock)

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

# AMD beats Q3 estimates on top and bottom line, offers strong Q4 guidance

[Daniel Howley](/author/daniel-howley)  · Technology Editor

Updated 3 min read

Advanced Micro Devices ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) [reported its Q3 earnings](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1265/amd-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) after the bell on Tuesday, topped analysts' expectations on earnings and revenue, and provided strong fourth quarter guidance.

The company said it foresees revenue of between $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion. Wall Street was anticipating revenue of $9.21 billion.

AMD stock rose in the immediate wake of the report, then reversed gains to fall 2% in early trading on Wednesday.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth," she added.

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share of $1.20 on revenue of $9.25 billion. Analysts were anticipating EPS of $1.17 on revenue of $8.74 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

AMD's data center revenue hit $4.3 billion. Analysts were expecting $4.1 billion. The company saw $3.5 billion in revenue in the same quarter last year.

AMD's client segment, which includes sales of laptop and desktop chips, saw revenue of $2.9 billion versus expectations of $2.6 billion.

AMD's gaming division pulled in $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for $1.1 billion.

AMD's report comes after the company announced a pair of massive AI chip deals with OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) and Oracle ([ORCL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ORCL/)).

Last month, AMD signed a deal to provide OpenAI with up to [6 gigawatts worth of graphics processing units (GPUs)](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-stock-rockets-higher-on-multibillion-dollar-openai-deal-125503782.html) to power its AI data centers. In turn, OpenAI agreed to purchase upwards of 160 million shares of AMD stock, equal to roughly 10% of the company.

Under its deal with Oracle, AMD will [deploy up to 50,000 GPUs](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amd-and-oracle-announce-agreement-for-50000-gpus-as-ai-deal-spree-continues-121807781.html) across the cloud company's data centers.

AMD is also providing chips to power two Department of Energy supercomputers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The systems will [represent a $1 billion public and private investment](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1264/amd-powers-u-s-sovereign-ai-factory-supercomputers-accelerating-an-open-american-ai-stack) when completed.

The moves have sent AMD stock rocketing 53% over the past month. Shares are up 108% year to date and 79% over the past 12 months as of Tuesday.

But AMD still trails Nvidia ([NVDA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/)), which owns the majority of the AI market and recently saw its market cap cross the $5 trillion mark. AMD's market cap sits at $418 billion.

*Read more:* [*Live coverage of corporate earnings*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/earnings-live-jpmorgan-citi-and-other-wall-street-banks-set-to-lead-off-q3-earnings-season-202336019.html)

OpenAI and Oracle will begin deploying AMD's next-generation MI450 line of GPUs and rack-scale platforms in the second half of 2026. Rack-scale offerings allow chips to be slotted into large collections of servers to operate as massive computing systems.

AMD's MI450 chips and rack-scale products will be an important part of the company's future growth strategy, Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore wrote in an analyst note.

"AMD's rack-scale solution shipping next year is the key, and we are excited to see what the company can do," Moore wrote prior to AMD's announcement.

"It's still early to make market share assessments, and while the Open AI agreement is clearly an accelerant, the reliance on cloud providers to ramp those 6 gigawatts still creates some uncertainty," he added. "Ultimately, to drive share gains, the company will need to provide better ROI than [Nvidia] can offer, and customers still raise questions about that given lower rack density and the need to resolve ecosystem issues."

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

**Segment Summary**

*   Data Center segment revenue was $4.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year primarily driven by strong demand for 5 th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

*   Client and Gaming segment revenue was $4 billion, up 73% year-over-year. Client revenue was a record $2.8 billion, up 46% year-over-year primarily driven by record sales of Ryzen™ processors and a richer product mix. Gaming revenue was $1.3 billion, up 181% year-over-year driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon™ gaming GPUs.

*   Embedded segment revenue was $857 million, down 8% year-over-year.

(1) The Company operates as three operating segments, Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded segments.

The Data Center segment primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers.

The Client and Gaming segment primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, and discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services.

The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products. 

From time to time, the Company may also sell or license portions of its IP portfolio. 

All Other category primarily includes certain expenses and credits that are not allocated to any of the operating segments, such as amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, employee stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer and restructuring charges.

The Company presents “Adjusted EBITDA” as a supplemental measure of its performance. Adjusted EBITDA for the Company is determined by adjusting GAAP net income for interest expense, other (income) expense, net, income tax provision (benefit), equity income in investee, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer, loss contingency on legal matter, and income from discontinued operations, net of tax. The Company calculates and presents Adjusted EBITDA because management believes it is of importance to investors and lenders in relation to its overall capital structure and its ability to borrow additional funds. In addition, the Company presents Adjusted EBITDA because it believes this measure assists investors in comparing its performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that the Company does not believe are indicative of its core operating performance. The Company’s calculation of Adjusted EBITDA may or may not be consistent with the calculation of this measure by other companies in the same industry. Investors should not view Adjusted EBITDA as an alternative to the GAAP operating measure of net income or GAAP liquidity measures of cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities. In addition, Adjusted EBITDA does not take into account changes in certain assets and liabilities that can affect cash flows.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

**Segment Summary**

*   Data Center segment revenue was $4.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year primarily driven by strong demand for 5 th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

*   Client and Gaming segment revenue was $4 billion, up 73% year-over-year. Client revenue was a record $2.8 billion, up 46% year-over-year primarily driven by record sales of Ryzen™ processors and a richer product mix. Gaming revenue was $1.3 billion, up 181% year-over-year driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon™ gaming GPUs.

*   Embedded segment revenue was $857 million, down 8% year-over-year.

**Recent PR Highlights**

*   Customer momentum for AMD AI platforms is accelerating:

    *   Vultr [announced](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250909530221/en/Vultr-Announces-Availability-of-AMD-Instinct-MI355X-GPUs-Worldwide) the global availability of AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs across its cloud platform.

    *   DigitalOcean [expanded](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Launches-New-Products-and-Innovations-at-Deploy-Conference/default.aspx) its AMD-based cloud offerings to support a broader range of AI workloads with AMD Instinct MI325X GPUs available now and AMD Instinct MI350X GPUs available later this year.

    *   AMD and Tech Mahindra [announced](https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-9-25-tech-mahindra-joins-hands-with-amd-to-drive-n.html) a collaboration to bring AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC processors to the Cloud BlazeTech enterprise AI solution.

    *   The Lux AI supercomputer, powered by AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Pensando advanced networking technologies, will be the first U.S. AI factory supercomputer.

    *   The Discovery supercomputer, expected to be delivered in 2028, will be based on next-gen AMD EPYC CPUs, codenamed “Venice,” and AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs, a new MI400 Series accelerator designed for sovereign AI and scientific computing.

*   AMD [released](https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/ecosystems-and-partners/rocm-7.0-blog/README.html) ROCm™ 7 software, boosting training and inference performance and expanding enterprise tools for infrastructure management and deployment.

*   AMD [announced](https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-10-27-amd-completes-divestiture-of-zt-systems-data-cente.html) the completion of the divestiture of the ZT Systems data center infrastructure manufacturing business to Sanmina.

*   AMD partners expanded their cloud offerings based on AMD EPYC processors to meet growing compute demand for enterprise and AI workloads:

    *   AWS [announced](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/epyc-on-aws-5th-gen-processors-power-high-performance.html) the availability of Amazon EC2 M8a general-purpose instance powered by 5 th Gen AMD EPYC processors, delivering up to 30% higher performance than the previous generation.

    *   Oracle [announced](https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/post/cloudatcustomer-privatecloudappliance-x11) next-gen Compute Cloud@Customer X11 and Private Cloud Appliance X11 platforms powered by 5 th Gen AMD EPYC processors.

*   IBM and AMD [announced](https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-8-26-ibm-and-amd-join-forces-to-build-the-future-o.html) plans to combine quantum computers and high-performance compute to drive scalable, open-source next-generation computing architectures.

*   AMD delivered new capabilities for the most demanding PC and gaming workloads, including:

    *   The [AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ 9000WX and Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9000X Series processors](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/workstations/ryzen-threadripper.html), delivering unmatched multi-core performance and platform capabilities for creators, enthusiasts and professionals.

    *   [AMD FSR 4](https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/technologies/fidelityfx/super-resolution.html), a ML-based upscaling technology that enhances frame rates and visuals, saw rapid adoption with supported games doubling since launch to over 85.

*   AMD expanded its x86 embedded processor portfolio, including:

    *   The [AMD EPYC Embedded 4005 series processors](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/amd-introduces-epyc-embedded-4005-processors-for-low.html), built to deliver performance, optimized system costs and extended deployment lifecycles in network security appliances and entry-level industrial edge servers.

    *   The [AMD Ryzen Embedded 9000 processors](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/amd-ryzen-embedded-9000-series-brings-next-gen-performa.html) delivering exceptional performance-per-watt, low latency, and the long-term stability for industrial PCs, automation systems and machine vision applications.

**Current Outlook**

AMD’s outlook statements are based on current expectations. The following statements are forward-looking and actual results could differ materially depending on market conditions and the factors set forth under “Cautionary Statement” below.

For the fourth quarter of 2025, AMD expects revenue to be approximately $9.6 billion, plus or minus $300 million. At the mid-point of the revenue range, this represents year-over-year growth of approximately 25% and sequential growth of approximately 4%. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be approximately 54.5%. Our current outlook does not include any revenue from AMD Instinct MI308 shipments to China.

(1) The Company operates as three operating segments, Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded segments.

The Data Center segment primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers.

The Client and Gaming segment primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, and discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services.

The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products. 

From time to time, the Company may also sell or license portions of its IP portfolio. 

All Other category primarily includes certain expenses and credits that are not allocated to any of the operating segments, such as amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, employee stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer and restructuring charges.

The Company presents “Adjusted EBITDA” as a supplemental measure of its performance. Adjusted EBITDA for the Company is determined by adjusting GAAP net income for interest expense, other (income) expense, net, income tax provision (benefit), equity income in investee, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer, loss contingency on legal matter, and income from discontinued operations, net of tax. The Company calculates and presents Adjusted EBITDA because management believes it is of importance to investors and lenders in relation to its overall capital structure and its ability to borrow additional funds. In addition, the Company presents Adjusted EBITDA because it believes this measure assists investors in comparing its performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that the Company does not believe are indicative of its core operating performance. The Company’s calculation of Adjusted EBITDA may or may not be consistent with the calculation of this measure by other companies in the same industry. Investors should not view Adjusted EBITDA as an alternative to the GAAP operating measure of net income or GAAP liquidity measures of cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

(1) The Company operates as three operating segments, Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded segments.

The Data Center segment primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers.

The Client and Gaming segment primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, and discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services.

The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products. 

From time to time, the Company may also sell or license portions of its IP portfolio. 

All Other category primarily includes certain expenses and credits that are not allocated to any of the operating segments, such as amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, employee stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer and restructuring charges.

The Company presents “Adjusted EBITDA” as a supplemental measure of its performance. Adjusted EBITDA for the Company is determined by adjusting GAAP net income for interest expense, other (income) expense, net, income tax provision (benefit), equity income in investee, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer, loss contingency on legal matter, and income from discontinued operations, net of tax. The Company calculates and presents Adjusted EBITDA because management believes it is of importance to investors and lenders in relation to its overall capital structure and its ability to borrow additional funds. In addition, the Company presents Adjusted EBITDA because it believes this measure assists investors in comparing its performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that the Company does not believe are indicative of its core operating performance. The Company’s calculation of Adjusted EBITDA may or may not be consistent with the calculation of this measure by other companies in the same industry. Investors should not view Adjusted EBITDA as an alternative to the GAAP operating measure of net income or GAAP liquidity measures of cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities. In addition, Adjusted EBITDA does not take into account changes in certain assets and liabilities that can affect cash flows.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

The Client and Gaming segment primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, and discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services.

The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products. 

From time to time, the Company may also sell or license portions of its IP portfolio. 

All Other category primarily includes certain expenses and credits that are not allocated to any of the operating segments, such as amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, employee stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related and other costs, inventory loss at (recovery from) contract manufacturer and restructuring charges.

The Company calculates and presents Adjusted EBITDA because management believes it is of importance to investors and lenders in relation to its overall capital structure and its ability to borrow additional funds. In addition, the Company presents Adjusted EBITDA because it believes this measure assists investors in comparing its performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that the Company does not believe are indicative of its core operating performance. The Company’s calculation of Adjusted EBITDA may or may not be consistent with the calculation of this measure by other companies in the same industry. Investors should not view Adjusted EBITDA as an alternative to the GAAP operating measure of net income or GAAP liquidity measures of cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities. In addition, Adjusted EBITDA does not take into account changes in certain assets and liabilities that can affect cash flows.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

**Segment Summary**

*   Data Center segment revenue was $4.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year primarily driven by strong demand for 5 th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

*   Client and Gaming segment revenue was $4 billion, up 73% year-over-year. Client revenue was a record $2.8 billion, up 46% year-over-year primarily driven by record sales of Ryzen™ processors and a richer product mix. Gaming revenue was $1.3 billion, up 181% year-over-year driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon™ gaming GPUs.

*   Embedded segment revenue was $857 million, down 8% year-over-year.

**Recent PR Highlights**

*   Customer momentum for AMD AI platforms is accelerating:

    *   OpenAI and AMD [announced](https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-10-6-amd-and-openai-announce-strategic-partnership-to-d.html) a strategic partnership where AMD will be a core preferred partner to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs to power OpenAI’s next generation AI infrastructure, with the first 1-gigawatt deployment of AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs set to begin in the second half of 2026.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

**Segment Summary**

*   Data Center segment revenue was $4.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year primarily driven by strong demand for 5 th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

*   Client and Gaming segment revenue was $4 billion, up 73% year-over-year. Client revenue was a record $2.8 billion, up 46% year-over-year primarily driven by record sales of Ryzen™ processors and a richer product mix. Gaming revenue was $1.3 billion, up 181% year-over-year driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon™ gaming GPUs.

*   Embedded segment revenue was $857 million, down 8% year-over-year.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 04, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter revenue was a record $9.2 billion, gross margin was 52%, operating income was $1.3 billion, net income was $1.2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $0.75. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.2 billion, net income was $2 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.20. Our third quarter results did not include any revenue from shipments of AMD Instinct™ MI308 GPU products to China.

"We delivered an outstanding quarter, with record revenue and profitability reflecting broad based demand for our high-performance EPYC and Ryzen processors and Instinct AI accelerators," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Our record third quarter performance and strong fourth quarter guidance marks a clear step up in our growth trajectory as our expanding compute franchise and rapidly scaling data center AI business drive significant revenue and earnings growth."

“We delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.2 billion, up 36% year-over-year, and generated record free cash flow, reflecting the strength of our leadership portfolio and disciplined execution,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our continued investments in AI and high-performance computing are driving significant growth and position AMD to deliver long-term value creation.”

**Segment Summary**

*   Data Center segment revenue was $4.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year primarily driven by strong demand for 5 th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

*   Client and Gaming segment revenue was $4 billion, up 73% year-over-year. Client revenue was a record $2.8 billion, up 46% year-over-year primarily driven by record sales of Ryzen™ processors and a richer product mix. Gaming revenue was $1.3 billion, up 181% year-over-year driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon™ gaming GPUs.

*   Embedded segment revenue was $857 million, down 8% year-over-year.

    *   Oracle [announced](https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/post/cloudatcustomer-privatecloudappliance-x11) next-gen Compute Cloud@Customer X11 and Private Cloud Appliance X11 platforms powered by 5 th Gen AMD EPYC processors.

*   AMD delivered new capabilities for the most demanding PC and gaming workloads, including:

    *   The [AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ 9000WX and Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9000X Series processors](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/workstations/ryzen-threadripper.html), delivering unmatched multi-core performance and platform capabilities for creators, enthusiasts and professionals.

    *   [AMD FSR 4](https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/technologies/fidelityfx/super-resolution.html), a ML-based upscaling technology that enhances frame rates and visuals, saw rapid adoption with supported games doubling since launch to over 85.

*   AMD expanded its x86 embedded processor portfolio, including:

    *   The [AMD EPYC Embedded 4005 series processors](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/amd-introduces-epyc-embedded-4005-processors-for-low.html), built to deliver performance, optimized system costs and extended deployment lifecycles in network security appliances and entry-level industrial edge servers.

    *   The [AMD Ryzen Embedded 9000 processors](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/amd-ryzen-embedded-9000-series-brings-next-gen-performa.html) delivering exceptional performance-per-watt, low latency, and the long-term stability for industrial PCs, automation systems and machine vision applications.

The gap rests on three things the market overestimates: durable growth, sustainable margins, and capital efficiency. My base case assumes 22% revenue growth, a steady 21% net margin, and sales-to-equity near 0.5x\u2014well below the platform\u2011like economics the price implies today.\\n\\n--\\n\\n**Executive summary**\\n---------------------\\n\\n*   **Company:** Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. \\n*   **Ticker:**[$AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)\\n*   **What I'm doing:** Avoiding \\n*   **Current price:** US$259.01 \\n*   **Estimated value:** US$55.51 \\n*   **Upside:** -78.6% \\n*   **Expected IRR:** 5.6% \\n\\n--\\n\\n**Investment thesis**\\n---------------------\\n\\nAMD at $259 per share on 5 November 2025 looks priced for perfection. I put fair value at roughly $56 and is why I'm avoiding. The gap rests son three things the market overestimates: durable growth, sustainable margins, and capital efficiency. My base case assumes 22% revenue growth, a steady 21% net margin, and sales-to-equity near 0.5x\u2014well below the platform\u2011like economics the price implies today.\\n\\nThe market is underwriting a very different future: a long\u2011run 34.7% revenue CAGR, a 33.2% net margin and a 0.8x sales\u2011to\u2011equity ratio. That bundle would make AMD look more like a software platform than a fabless chip designer that must keep pace with Nvidia and depend on foundry supply. I do not see evidence for it.\\n\\nGrowth first. AI demand is real, but ramps are lumpy and constrained. Nvidia still dominates accelerators and export controls limit China\u2011bound SKUs. Recent prints point to moderation, not acceleration: AMD\u2019s Data Center segment grew 22% year on year in Q3 2025, and management\u2019s Q4 set\u2011up implies growth in the mid\u201120s with gross margins in the mid\u201150s, not a re\u2011acceleration to the mid\u201130s that the market\u2019s curve assumes. A 22% through\u2011cycle path is still strong, just not fantasy.\\n\\nMargins next. To earn 33% net margins, AMD would need Nvidia\u2011like pricing power and lighter operating expense intensity. That jars with the firm\u2019s heavy, ongoing R&D and software investment as it pushes ROCm and an accelerator roadmap (MI300/MI350 to MI400). 2024 GAAP gross margin was about 49%, and non\u2011GAAP gross margin was 54% in Q3 2025\u2014good progress, but not the operating leverage one needs to convert into a one\u2011third net margin through the cycle. I anchor on a 21% steady margin instead.\\n\\nCapital efficiency seals it. After big acquisitions, goodwill and intangibles keep equity large relative to sales. Working capital needs for accelerators are rising, and even with buybacks I expect sales\u2011to\u2011equity to settle near 0.5x rather than the market\u2019s 0.8x. That matters because it governs how quickly the company can grow without bloating the balance sheet. History since the acquisitions sits in the mid\u20110.3s to mid\u20110.4s; 0.5x already assumes improvement.\\n\\nWhen I run these economics through a DCF, I get an intrinsic value of $36\u2013$66 per share, with a base case of $55.51. Even the 90th percentile of simulated values lands near $83\u2014miles below the current price. The reverse\u2011DCF embedded in today\u2019s quote delivers an expected IRR of just 5.6%, which is thin for a business facing this much competitive heat and execution risk.\\n\\nSimple cross\u2011checks say the same. On prevailing numbers AMD trades at 72x earnings, 16x sales, and 5.6x book\u2014rich even for AI\u2011exposed semis. If I apply a fair 12\u201316x earnings multiple to consensus EPS of about $5.10, I get $61\u2013$82 per share, remarkably close to the DCF\u2019s generous end and still far below $259. The signal is consistent: the equity embeds too much growth, too much margin, and too much efficiency.\\n\\nNear\u2011term events could start to close the gap. In late January 2026 (unconfirmed), Q4 2025 results and 2026 guidance may frame growth in the low\u201120s with net margins below 30%. That alone could take 20\u201330% off the share price as models converge with reality. Around mid\u2011March 2026 (unconfirmed), the annual report should reveal sales\u2011to\u2011equity nearer 0.45\u20130.50, undercutting 0.8x efficiency assumptions. Early 2026 results (around May, unconfirmed) are likely to show gross margins in the low\u2011to\u2011mid\u201150s with elevated opex to fund the roadmap\u2014again inconsistent with a one\u2011third net margin. These are tests I expect AMD to \u201cpass\u201d in a way that supports the bear case.\\n\\nRisks to my view are clear. A faster AI cycle, stronger MI350/MI400 ramps, and broader ROCm adoption could pull demand forward and lift pricing and mix. In that upside world, growth could skew toward the mid\u201130s, net margins could approach 30%+, and sales\u2011to\u2011equity could rise toward 0.7\u20130.8. Depending on how far those drivers run, the shares could justify the $220\u2013$300 range\u2014or even $300\u2013$350 if accelerators and EPYC both surprise and sentiment re\u2011rates. I do not assign high probability to that path today, but I respect it.\\n\\nWhat would change my mind? Consistent, audited evidence of capital efficiency trending to 0.7\u20130.8x; non\u2011GAAP gross margins holding mid\u201150s while opex intensity falls, lifting the net margin toward the high\u201120s; and proof that ROCm has become a sticky software layer that improves pricing power. If two of the three show up in reported numbers, I would raise my margin and efficiency anchors and soften the stance.\\n\\nUntil then, I stick with the simple story.
